result:
This is probably the known `$.model.fork` problem: on a resumed session's first command, it answers `nothing-to-fork`. I'm assuming that's what you mean by "fork" here, since this repo's `AGENTS.md` documents exactly that case. If you meant the Agent tool's fork subagent, tell me and I'll look at that instead.

The repo already handles it. `bws-kit/classify-fork.ts` (`runFork`, lines 108–129) does this:

1. Calls `$.model.fork`.
2. If the reply is `nothing-to-fork`, reads `$.session.messages()`.
3. Builds a transcript and calls `$.model.complete` on the session's model (`$.session.model()`), with the same timeout and signal.
4. Returns `via: 'complete'` on that path, or `nothing-to-fork` if there are no messages at all.

The `bws-kit` tests in `tests/classify-fork.test.ts` (around lines 125–150) cover both branches. The mods that use it (`bws-memory`, `bws-direction`, `bws-diagram`) vendor their own copies under `hooks/kit/`, so a fix has to go into the kit and then be synced with `python tools/sync-kit.py --plugin <mod>`.

Two things I did not check:

- I read the code and didn't run the tests or a live session, so I can't say the fallback works end to end after a resume.
- The mods that call `$.model.fork` directly, `bws-memory/hooks/register.tsx:121` and `bws-diagram/hooks/register.tsx:67`, pass `fork` straight through. They get the fallback only if they call `runFork`. I haven't confirmed that every path goes through it.

If you're seeing a failure, send me the mod and the symptom (an error message, or the `--debug` log around the resumed command). I can then run `runFork`'s tests or reproduce it with `tools/live.py`.
